facts.claim: The Google facade streams Chat Completions for AI Studio and Vertex AI targets through the core Runtime's Stream, which core's Google reads from streamGenerateContent, and hands the API layer each Chat chunk's data without [DONE]; at v1.7.0 its Stream returned a ConfigError, which the API answered with 502. A stream whose caller leaves ends with the caller's context error, one with a record over the size limit ends with StreamRecordTooLargeError, and any other failure maps as a completion's failure does. The characterization golden for an AI Studio Chat stream records a 200 event stream ending in [DONE] where it recorded that 502, and an API test streams a Gemini function call as a tool call delta with its thought signature, the finish reason tool_calls and the usage the client asked for, which the gateway records.

googleChatPayload sends Google the messages, max_tokens (max_completion_tokens or the internal _max_output_tokens when max_tokens is unset), temperature, tools and tool_choice, and stream_options on a stream; at v1.7.0 the facade sent the messages, the output limit and temperature only. googleChatField reads the request: tools count as sent when every tool is a function tool with a name and parameters that are an object or absent, and tool_choice when it is auto, none, required with a function declared, or a declared function. Any other tools or tool choice count as unsent, and the API layer refuses a request that carries an unsent field with 400 before anything reaches Google, as an API test shows for tool_choice required without tools.

The effective provider registry, core's manifest with the gateway's overlay, lists 57 entries where v1.7.0 listed 27: llmgw-core v1.8.0 adds 30, among them DeepSeek, Moonshot AI (Kimi), Zhipu BigModel, Z.ai, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Qwen), Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan, Volcengine Ark, SiliconFlow, NVIDIA NIM, ModelScope, MiniMax, LiteLLM, vLLM and LM Studio. Of the 30, 28 run as openai_compatible and 2, the Coding Plan's Anthropic-compatible wires, as anthropic, runtime types TestProviderRegistryIsUniqueAndRunnable requires the gateway to build; 11 offer no model discovery. The four Alibaba Cloud Coding Plan entries are personal-only with risk level red, and NVIDIA NIM and the two ModelScope entries are yellow. The registry comes from the llmgw-core module: in the gateway only registry_snapshot.json, which a test reads, and the count in registry_test.go changed.

openAICoreProvider.NativeSurfaces returns the surfaces core lists for a model core serves without Chat Completions, such as an OVHcloud AI Endpoints NVR voice, so the audio handlers send that model's speech through core, whose OVHcloud NVR client in llmgw-core v1.9.0 posts it to the voice's own host and answers with WAV. For a model with Chat Completions it drops the audio surfaces as at v1.7.0, so the gateway proxies that model's audio itself; a test shows both on one OVHcloud instance.

go/go.mod requires github.com/xibodev/llmgw-core v1.9.0 where v1.7.0 required v1.6.0; llm-translate v0.4.0, llm-provider-auth v1.0.1 and every other requirement are as at v1.7.0, and go/go.sum changes only llmgw-core's two lines. go mod tidy -diff reports nothing to change and go mod verify verifies every module.

llmgw-core v1.9.0 classes a 402 refusal as billing, and a 4xx whose body cites quota, the context length, or tools or images the model does not take as billing, context_overflow, tools_unsupported or media_unsupported. The OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Google, Ollama and companion daemon facades map an upstream refusal by its status before they read core's class, so retries, failover, circuits and the error a client reads follow the status for these refusals as for any other. Tests pin this for each reason on the OpenAI-compatible facade's four operations, for billing and a context overflow on Google, for billing and a long prompt on Anthropic and for unsupported tools on Ollama; under a mutation that reads core's class first these tests fail, where the tests at v1.7.0 caught only Google's billing refusal.

Core reads a gateway InvocationError with status 402 as class billing, which the classification test pins. Only execution.Execute records that class, in the attempts of its result; the router's walk passes a zero Executor and reads only the value and candidate Execute returns, so the Admission and CredentialFailover llmgw-core v1.9.0 adds stay off. The provider circuits observe outcomes through observeCircuit, which sets no class, and the gateway never calls the core Runtime's Health.

The gateway sets neither the Headers llmgw-core v1.7.0 adds to the Anthropic, Google, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, ElevenLabs and MiMo configurations nor OpenAICompatibleConfig.Registry from v1.8.0, and builds providers with its own factory rather than providers.Build or runtime.RegistryProviders, so those additions leave its requests as they were.

evidence.source: go/internal (no Headers or Registry configuration field set, no call to providers.Build or runtime.RegistryProviders)

conclusion.summary: The release streams Google AI Studio and Vertex AI chat and sends function tools to Gemini, offers 30 more registry providers, speaks through OVHcloud AI Endpoints' NVR voices, and takes llmgw-core v1.9.0, whose new refusal classes the facades read by status. No non-test file under go/internal/api, the CLI, IAM, configuration, the router or the console changed. Every accepted proposition holds for this source; none rests on an implementation this release changed, and the exploratory run, the unit tests, the race run and the Docker acceptance exercise them.
